o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish درمان (dermān), from Persian درمان (darmân).

From Proto-Turkic *yan- (“to burn (intr.), blaze up”).Turkish yanmak, Crimean Tatar yanmaq (“to burn”), Bashkir яныу (yanıw, “to burn”), Chuvash ҫунма (śunma, “to burn, shine, worry, suffer”), Kazakh жану (januw, “to burn”), Kyrgyz жануу (januu, “to burn”), Turkmen ýanmak (“to be burnt”), Uzbek yonmoq (“to ignite, glow”), Yakut сандаар (sandaar, “to shine”) (< caus. *jan-tɨr-).
Borrowed from Classical Persian عبادتخانه ('ibādatxāna). By surface analysis, ibadət + -xana.
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish آیریلق (ayrılıq). By surface analysis, ayrı + -lıq.
